lines.text: For forty years they tried. Nine times they came knocking on the door of the World Cup. Nine times it stayed shut.
Tonight, for the very first time, a tiny kingdom walks out onto the biggest stage on Earth. And in the stands, one old dreamer is finally living the day he never thought he'd see.
Last time, we predicted Iraq and Norway would draw one-all. Tonight: the dreamers... against the ghosts of a golden age.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-three. Austria versus Jordan. Old European royalty... against the bravest newcomers in the world.
And stay with me — because the story of how Jordan got here is one of the great fairytales of modern football.
First, the history. And it is true. Austria once had a team they simply called the Wunderteam — the wonder team.
In the nineteen-thirties they tore Europe apart. Six-nil over Germany. Eight-one over Switzerland. Football like nobody had seen.
Their heartbeat was Matthias Sindelar — so graceful they called him the Mozart of Football.
They reached a World Cup semifinal in nineteen thirty-four. And then... they fell. Austria have never, not once, won a World Cup.
Nearly a century of waiting for the wonder team's heirs. That is the weight Austria carry tonight.
And across from them — Jordan. The Nashama. The Brave Ones. Until now, only ever a nearly-team.
But two years ago, they wrote something nobody can take back. The twenty twenty-three Asian Cup.
In the semifinal they faced South Korea — sixty places above them in the world. Jordan won. Two-nil. Al-Naimat, then Al-Tamari.
A nation that had never reached a final... was suddenly in one. They lost it to Qatar — but the world had seen them now.
And then they did the impossible. After forty years and nine failed campaigns, Jordan qualified for their first ever World Cup.
Now, Austria. Led by David Alaba — a defender who has won everything in the club game, captaining the heirs of the Wunderteam.
Marcel Sabitzer drives the midfield. Konrad Laimer never stops running. Christoph Baumgartner arrives late in the box.
And Marko Arnautović — the old fox up front, still dangerous, still smiling.
But Jordan have weapons too. Musa Al-Tamari — quick, fearless, the man who lit up that Asian Cup.
And Yazan Al-Naimat, the striker who scores on the nights that matter most.
So here is the duel. Austrian experience and pedigree... against the fearless joy of a nation with nothing to lose.
Our prediction — built on Austrian steel, on a century of hurt that demands an answer, and on a debut that refuses to be quiet. Watch.
Austria press early. Sabitzer threads it, Baumgartner times his run — and slides it home. One-nil, Austria.
But you do not tell the Brave Ones it's over. Al-Tamari drives at the heart of it, lays it off — Al-Naimat. One-all. Jordan dream out loud.
Then Austria's pedigree speaks. A corner, Alaba climbs — and the heirs of the Wunderteam find the winner. Two-one.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. Austria edge it. But Jordan walk off to an ovation — they belonged.
Do you agree? Comment WUNDERTEAM if Austria's class is too much. Comment NASHAMA if you back the brave to shock the world.
And that old dreamer in the stands? Legend number twenty-three: the Keeper of the Dream. Forty years he waited for this.
He kept a ticket from every campaign that failed — and tonight, finally, he has the one that didn't. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes. Hit like, send this to a friend, and subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
